decision. Follow the rest of `AGENTS.md` and `PRINCIPLES.md` (non-negotiables: no `unwrap`/`expect` in lib code, every `pub`
item documented, `String::with_capacity`, `BTreeMap` for output maps, char-boundary truncation, tests via `cargo nextest`).

1. `git fetch origin && git checkout -B <your-branch> origin/main` (branch name is in your task).
2. TDD: failing test first (confirm it fails for the right reason), then implement, then green.

   integrator consolidates them.

   `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the Callisto docs). Package `michi-core`; the fixed group releases everything together.
   Start a paragraph with `Breaking:` if rendered output of existing calls changes.
6. Checks, judged by exit code only (never by reading output): `just fmt-check`, `just clippy`, `just test-rust`,
   `just typos`, and `just semver` if it exists. Report which you ran and which you did not.
7. Commit (conventional message, why-not-what). **No claude.ai session links, no `Claude-Session` trailer.** Push the branch
   and open a **draft** PR against main with a short plain body (what, why, checked, not run). Never merge, never force-push,
   never push to main.

Bash runs in a sandbox. Cargo (registry cache writes), `git commit` (a pre-commit hook), and `git push` need
`dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` on that one command. Use `$TMPDIR` for temp files, not `/tmp`. Prefix shell commands
with `rtk` if the hook does not already. Keep commands simple (no `$(...)`-computed git arguments).

- New modules: `section.rs` (slice A), `budget.rs` and `provenance.rs` (slice B). Re-export from `lib.rs` with explicit
  `pub use` lists (no globs). Touch `lib.rs` only for your own module and re-exports.

- Render order for a response: sections in insertion order, then `budget:`, then `provenance:`, then `help[]`, then `recovery[]`.
- Render functions always succeed; they never panic.
- JSON stays hand-built and `serde_json`-free in the default build (reuse the existing JSON string escaping helper in
  `response.rs`); `serde`/`schemars` derives only behind the existing features.

`truncation(&outcome, guidance)` sets the count and the cut hint in one call, so `totalCount` and `help[]` always describe the same cut. It does not touch the rows: `AgentResponse` holds TOON `Value` rows, not the caller's `T`, so pass `outcome.kept` (converted) to `.items(...)`. A later `.total_count()` or `.hints()` still overrides it.

`total_count` applies to both paths. On the KV path with no items the body is just `totalCount: N` (the free `render_kv` still returns `""` for empty items), so a count the caller set is never dropped; with neither items nor a count the body is empty.

### Budget and provenance types (`budget`, `provenance`)

Plain data types for the envelope in [07-wisp-and-monokl-envelope.md](07-wisp-and-monokl-envelope.md) §2 and §3. All four are `#[non_exhaustive]`, derive `Debug`, `Clone`, `Default` (where it makes sense), `PartialEq` and `Eq`, and have builder methods. Behind `serde` they derive `Serialize` with camelCase keys (absent `Option`s skipped); behind `schemars` they derive `JsonSchema`.

- `BudgetSummary`: optional `max_tokens`, `max_bytes`, `max_items`, `tokens_used`, `bytes_used`; `truncated: bool`; `sections: Vec<SectionCost>`. Builders: `new`, `max_tokens`, `max_bytes`, `max_items`, `tokens_used`, `bytes_used`, `truncated`, `section`.
- `SectionCost`: `name`, `returned`, optional `total`, `truncated`. Builders: `new(name, returned)`, `total`, `truncated`.
- `ProvenanceBlock`: ordered `entries: Vec<ProvenanceEntry>` and optional `fingerprint`. Builders: `new`, `entry(label, value)`, `fingerprint`.
- `ProvenanceEntry`: `label`, `value`; `new(label, value)`.

Rendering is crate-private for now and is wired into `AgentResponse` separately. The `budget:` block lists `tokensUsed`, `bytesUsed`, `maxTokens`, `maxBytes`, `maxItems` when set, then `truncated`; the `sections[n]{name,returned,total,truncated}:` roll-up follows only when asked for, and an unknown `total` is a `null` cell. The `provenance:` block lists entries in order, then `fingerprint`. Labels are encoded as TOON keys and values as TOON strings, so newlines and colons in caller text cannot start a line of their own.

### Sections (`section`)

A response can hold several blocks. `AgentResponse::section(Section)` appends one; sections render in insertion order, after the `items()` / `kv_items()` slot when one was set, and before `help[]` and `recovery[]`. The caller owns the order.

1	# The Wisp / monokl Response Envelope
2	
3	> **Status: Proposed.** This design is not implemented. The inclusion case remains open; see the notes below.
4	
5	This proposal describes how one `AgentResponse` could carry a monokl batch result or Wisp briefing: named sections, budget and provenance summaries, and index-bearing operation outcomes.
6	
7	This is the michi half of a contract written down in three places. monokl's `docs/spec/08-library-session-api.md` §7 defines the batch `QueryResponse`; Wisp's `docs/02-architecture-and-contracts.md` §11–§12 defines the MCP surface that renders it; this doc defines what michi must hold for either of them to render through it. Nothing here changes how michi serializes MCP — that part is already right.
8	
9	## The gap
10	
11	`AgentResponse` today holds exactly one body. From `crates/michi-core/src/response.rs`:
12	
13	| Field / type | Line | What it constrains |
14	| --- | --- | --- |
15	| `toon: ToonOptions` | 34 | One TOON slot: one `type_name` for the whole response, one `fields`/`rows` table |
16	| `single_item: Vec<KvItem>` | 36 | One KV slot |
17	| `toon.total_count: Option<usize>` | 34 | One count, for whichever slot renders |
18	| `enum RenderTarget { Unset, Toon, Kv }` | 18–22 | The two slots are mutually exclusive |
19	| `toon.max_cell_len: usize` | 34 | Per-cell clamp, TOON path only, set by `truncate_cells_at()` (`DEFAULT_TRUNCATE_CELLS = 200`, line 25) |
20	
21	`items()` (line 59) sets `target = RenderTarget::Toon`; `kv_items()` (line 108) sets `Kv`; `body()` (line 194) dispatches on `target`, so `render()` reads whichever setter ran last. Calling both silently drops one. A ten-operation batch is not expressible: nine sections disappear with no error and no signal that they existed.
22	
23	The truncation model has the same shape problem one level down. `truncate_cells_at` clamps a cell. `michi_core::truncate::Truncated { content, original_chars, removed }` describes a string. `michi_core::truncation::TruncationOutcome` describes one list, and `AgentResponse::truncation()` turns it into the response's `totalCount` and one `help[]` line. None describes a response of several parts. The only envelope-level "there is more" signal is `total_count: Option<usize>` plus free-text hints — a bare integer with no per-section breakdown, no relation to a budget, and no way to say why anything was dropped. monokl's `BudgetReport` would have to be flattened into free-text `hint()` calls to reach the agent at all.
24	
25	## What gets added
26	
27	Five additions, in dependency order. All five are pure michi and always compiled — nothing here reaches outside the michi workspace for a type. The fourth changes an existing rendered format; the fifth extends `structured_content`.
28	
29	### 1. Repeatable sections
30	
31	```rust
32	/// One named block within a response. A response may hold any number.
33	#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
34	#[non_exhaustive]
35	pub struct Section {
36	    /// The section's type name — the identifier at the head of its TOON line, or the KV block's label.
37	    pub name: String,
38	    /// The section's contents.
39	    pub body: SectionBody,
40	    /// How many items this section actually carries.
41	    pub returned_count: usize,
42	    /// How many existed before truncation. `Some(n)` with `n > returned_count` is the "there is more" signal.
43	    pub total_count: Option<usize>,
44	    /// Whether producing this section dropped anything.
45	    pub truncated: bool,
46	}
47	
48	#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
49	#[non_exhaustive]
50	pub enum SectionBody {
51	    /// A uniform list. Rendered through `michi_core::toon::ToonOptions`, per-cell truncation applied.
52	    Toon { fields: Vec<String>, rows: Vec<Vec<Value>> },
53	    /// A single receipt or a small set of labelled scalars.
54	    Kv(Vec<KvItem>),
55	    /// Prose or an already-rendered fragment michi passes through unchanged.
56	    Text(String),
57	}
58	
59	impl Section {
60	    pub fn toon(name: impl Into<String>, fields: Vec<String>, rows: Vec<Vec<Value>>) -> Self;
61	    pub fn kv(name: impl Into<String>, items: Vec<KvItem>) -> Self;
62	    pub fn text(name: impl Into<String>, body: impl Into<String>) -> Self;
63	    /// Record the pre-truncation count. `total_count(Some(n))` with `n > returned_count` renders `totalCount: n`.
64	    pub fn total_count(self, total: Option<usize>) -> Self;
65	    pub fn truncated(self, truncated: bool) -> Self;
66	}
67	
68	impl AgentResponse {
69	    /// Append a section. Sections render in insertion order — the caller owns ordering,
70	    /// because ordering is a policy the caller A/Bs (Wisp D-018), not something michi decides.
71	    #[must_use]
72	    pub fn section(self, s: Section) -> Self;
73	}
74	```
75	
76	`items()` and `kv_items()` stay, as one-section sugar over the same storage: `items(rows, fields)` becomes `section(Section::toon(self.toon.type_name.clone(), fields, rows))`, `kv_items(items)` becomes `section(Section::kv(self.toon.type_name.clone(), items))`. `RenderTarget` survives as the record of which sugar was used, because `render_toon()` and `render_kv()` are documented to read their named slot unconditionally regardless of the last setter (AC-009) and that behavior has to hold.
77	
78	Two invariants keep this compatible with what already ships:
79	
80	- **A response with zero or one section renders byte-for-byte as it does today**, on every one of `render(Text)`, `render(Json)`, `render_toon()`, `render_kv()`, and `render_for()`. The existing `insta` snapshots are the test for this; if any of them moves, the change is wrong. Per the SemVer table in [05-scope-and-quality.md](05-scope-and-quality.md) a rendered-output change is a major bump, and multi-section support does not have to be one.
81	- **`returned_count` is derived, not trusted, for `Toon` and `Kv` bodies.** Render functions always succeed ([`PRINCIPLES.md`](../../PRINCIPLES.md)), so a `returned_count` disagreeing with `rows.len()` / `items.len()` is clamped to the real length with a `debug_assert!` alongside — the assert fires under `cargo nextest`, the clamp runs in release. `Text` bodies keep whatever the caller declared, since michi cannot count items in prose.
82	
83	Rendered, a two-section response is just the sections in order:
84	
85	```text
86	brief.symbols[12]{name,kind,file,line}:
87	  RetryPolicy,struct,src/retry/policy.rs,14
88	  …
89	totalCount: 40
90	brief.refs[5]{symbol,file,line}:
91	  RetryPolicy,src/http/client.rs,88
92	  …
93	```
94	
95	### 2. A response-level budget report
96	
97	```rust
98	/// What a budget block renders: the ceilings a caller was working under, what the response cost
99	/// against them, and what that cost each section. michi owns this type and names nothing from
100	/// Wisp or monokl.
101	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
102	#[non_exhaustive]
103	pub struct BudgetSummary {
104	    /// Ceilings the caller set. Any of the three may be absent.
105	    pub max_tokens: Option<u64>,
106	    pub max_bytes: Option<u64>,
107	    pub max_items: Option<u64>,
108	    /// What the response cost, as the caller measured it.
109	    pub tokens_used: Option<u64>,
110	    pub bytes_used: Option<u64>,
111	    /// Whether the budget forced anything out of the response.
112	    pub truncated: bool,
113	    /// Per-section accounting, rendered in the order given.
114	    pub sections: Vec<SectionCost>,
115	}
116	
117	/// One section's line in the budget roll-up.
118	#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
119	#[non_exhaustive]
120	pub struct SectionCost {
121	    pub name: String,
122	    pub returned: u64,
123	    /// How many existed before truncation, when the caller knows.
124	    pub total: Option<u64>,
125	    pub truncated: bool,
126	}
127	
128	impl AgentResponse {
129	    /// Attach the response-level budget summary. One per response — a batch has one budget.
130	    #[must_use]
131	    pub fn budget(self, b: BudgetSummary) -> Self;
132	}
133	```
134	
135	Every number is an `Option` or a plain counter, so a caller who measured only tokens fills two fields and leaves the rest empty. `u64` rather than `usize` because these values reach JSON, where a platform-dependent width means nothing.
136	
137	Rendered once, after the last section, as a `budget:` KV block, with a roll-up naming each section's returned and total counts:
138	
139	```text
140	budget:
141	  tokensUsed: 7412
142	  bytesUsed: 31208
143	  maxTokens: 8000
144	  maxBytes: 2097152
145	  truncated: true
146	sections[2]{name,returned,total,truncated}:
147	  brief.symbols,12,40,true
148	  brief.refs,5,5,false
149	```
150	
151	Absent fields are omitted rather than rendered as `null`. The roll-up renders only when the response carries two or more sections. A single-section response already states its count in its own TOON header and `totalCount:` line, and repeating it costs tokens for nothing.
152	
153	michi renders a budget; it never computes one. Which items survive a budget is the caller's decision — a BM25 cutoff, a reserved-floor allocator, monokl's `apply_budget` degrade-then-drop ladder. Reporting what got cut in a consistent agent-readable shape is the part every caller needs identically, which is exactly the split [`PRINCIPLES.md`](../../PRINCIPLES.md) describes for truncation.
154	
155	### 3. A provenance slot
156	
157	```rust
158	/// What a provenance block renders: a short ordered list of labelled values, plus the one string
159	/// a freshness check compares. michi assigns no meaning to any of them.
160	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
161	#[non_exhaustive]
162	pub struct ProvenanceBlock {
163	    /// Rendered in order, one `label: value` line each.
164	    pub entries: Vec<ProvenanceEntry>,
165	    /// Rendered last when present.
166	    pub fingerprint: Option<String>,
167	}
168	
169	#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
170	#[non_exhaustive]
171	pub struct ProvenanceEntry {
172	    pub label: String,
173	    pub value: String,
174	}
175	
176	impl AgentResponse {
177	    /// Attach the provenance block this response was computed against.
178	    /// One per response: a batch runs against one snapshot, so it has one provenance.
179	    #[must_use]
180	    pub fn provenance(self, p: ProvenanceBlock) -> Self;
181	}
182	```
183	
184	A named pair rather than a `(String, String)` tuple: a tuple serializes as a two-element array, and a third-party reader of `structuredContent` then has nothing to key on.
185	
186	Rendered as a KV block after `budget:`:
187	
188	```text
189	provenance:
190	  analyzer: rust-analyzer@0.3.2
191	  observedAt: 1756950000000
192	  precision: exact
193	  fingerprint: b3f1c0d2e4a58691
194	```
195	
196	One block per response, not one per row — monokl's batch executes against a single `Snapshot`, so one fingerprint covers all N results rather than N fingerprints. Wisp's freshness tool (`wisp_check`) compares exactly the string in `fingerprint`.
197	
198	The caller picks the labels. `monokl-agent` fills them from the `wisp_contracts::Provenance` its snapshot carries, `wisp-output` from the same type on Wisp's side, and a tool with no analyzer at all fills two entries and no fingerprint. michi renders what it was handed and validates none of it.
199	
200	Per-edge precision stays out of the envelope. monokl carries `CapabilityPrecision` on each `DependencyEdge` and each `OpBudget` because a batch spanning an `Exact` TypeScript `refs` and a `Structural` Rust `dependents` has no honest single precision. michi renders whatever precision the caller wrote into a row or a provenance entry; it does not reduce several of them to one response-level value, and it has no type that could hold such a value.
201	
202	### 4. Per-op outcomes: `PartialSuccess`, widened
203	
204	`idempotency::PartialSuccess` already has the completed/failed/skipped trichotomy a batch needs. What it lacks is position: `Vec<String>` cannot express `results[i]` ↔ `ops[i]`, which is the ordering contract the batch API is built on (DataLoader's rule, restated in monokl §7.4 as an invariant). Reuse the type, widen the identifiers:
205	
206	```rust
207	/// One operation's identity within a batch.
208	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
209	#[non_exhaustive]
210	pub struct OpRef {
211	    /// Position in the caller's op slice. `results[index]` answers `ops[index]`.
212	    pub index: usize,
213	    /// Display name for the operation.
214	    pub operation: String,
215	    /// A stable machine token — `budget_exhausted`, `deadline`, `not_indexed` — never prose.
216	    /// michi does not define the vocabulary; the caller does.
217	    pub reason: Option<String>,
218	}
219	
220	pub struct PartialSuccess {
221	    pub completed: Vec<OpRef>,   // was Vec<String>
222	    pub failed: Vec<FailedOp>,
223	    pub skipped: Vec<OpRef>,     // was Vec<String>
224	}
225	
226	pub struct FailedOp {
227	    /// Position in the caller's op slice.
228	    pub index: usize,            // new
229	    pub operation: String,
230	    pub reason: String,
231	    pub recovery: Option<RecoveryHint>,
232	}
233	```
234	
235	The index becomes a rendered column, so the correspondence survives into what the agent reads:
236	
237	```text
238	partial_success: "2 completed, 1 failed, 1 skipped"
239	completed[2]{index,operation}:
240	  0,symbols
241	  1,dependents
242	failed[1]{index,operation,reason}:
243	  2,refs,"symbol not found: RetryPolicy"
244	skipped[1]{index,operation,reason}:
245	  3,search,budget_exhausted
246	```
247	
248	**This one is a major bump.** Today's `completed[2]: a,b` inline array becomes `completed[2]{index,operation}:`, so existing rendered output differs — the SemVer table calls that major, and the exact-output tests in `idempotency.rs` (AC-032, AC-033) and the `snapshot_partial_success_full` insta snapshot change with it. There is no external consumer to break yet, which is the cheapest moment this change will ever have.
249	
250	`exit_code()` is unchanged: `0` when nothing failed, `1` when anything did.
251	
252	### 5. `structured_content` and a published `outputSchema`
253	
254	`to_call_tool_result()` already builds `structured_content` from `render(OutputFormat::Json)`. Extend that JSON to carry the envelope:
255	
256	```json
257	{
258	  "body": "…",
259	  "sections": [
260	    {
261	      "name": "brief.symbols",
262	      "kind": "toon",
263	      "fields": ["name", "kind", "file", "line"],
264	      "rows": [["RetryPolicy", "struct", "src/retry/policy.rs", 14]],
265	      "returnedCount": 12,
266	      "totalCount": 40,
267	      "truncated": true
268	    }
269	  ],
270	  "budget": {
271	    "tokensUsed": 7412,
272	    "bytesUsed": 31208,
273	    "maxTokens": 8000,
274	    "truncated": true,
275	    "sections": []
276	  },
277	  "provenance": {
278	    "entries": [{ "label": "analyzer", "value": "rust-analyzer@0.3.2" }],
279	    "fingerprint": "b3f1c0d2e4a58691"
280	  },
281	  "hints": ["…"],
282	  "recovery": [],
283	  "isError": false
284	}
285	```
286	
287	Every key in that object is camelCase — `returnedCount`, `totalCount`, `tokensUsed`, `maxTokens`, `isError`. The rendered examples above are the specification of that, not an illustration of it: a third-party harness plugin reading this JSON without linking any Rust is a first-class consumer, and `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` on every envelope type is what keeps the spelling stable. Labels inside `provenance.entries` are caller-supplied strings and michi does not case-convert them.
288	
289	`sections`, `budget`, and `provenance` appear only when their slots are set. A response built entirely through today's API still emits exactly `body`, `hints`, `recovery`, `isError` — the four keys AC-004 pins — so that criterion needs its assertion rewritten from "exactly this set" to "exactly this set, plus the envelope keys whose slots were set", not deleted.
290	
291	The schema is published through the existing `schemars` feature: `Section`, `SectionBody`, `BudgetSummary`, `SectionCost`, `ProvenanceBlock`, and `ProvenanceEntry` derive `JsonSchema`, and the server declares the result as its tool's `outputSchema`. MCP makes conformance binding once a schema is declared — servers MUST return conforming structured results, clients SHOULD validate — which is the reason to publish one rather than leave the shape implicit. The token-budget caveat in [06-decisions.md](06-decisions.md) still applies: `outputSchema` enters the context window at `tools/list` time, so declare it on always-loaded tools, not on deferred ones.
292	
293	## The render path
294	
295	```mermaid
296	flowchart TB
297	    S1["Section — Toon"]
298	    S2["Section — Kv"]
299	    SN["Section — Text"]
300	    B["BudgetSummary"]
301	    P["ProvenanceBlock"]
302	    HR["hints / recovery"]
303	
304	    S1 --> AR
305	    S2 --> AR
306	    SN --> AR
307	    B --> AR
308	    P --> AR
309	    HR --> AR
310	
311	    AR["AgentResponse — N sections"]
312	
313	    AR -->|"render_text()"| text["sections in order, then budget:, provenance:, help[], recovery[]"]
314	    AR -->|"render(OutputFormat::Json)"| json["sections[], budget, provenance, hints, recovery, isError"]
315	
316	    text --> block["ContentBlock { audience: [assistant] }"]
317	    human["human_content()"] --> ublock["ContentBlock { audience: [user] }"]
318	
319	    block --> ctr["mcp::CallToolResult"]
320	    ublock --> ctr
321	    json --> ctr
322	    ctr --> wire["MCP tools/call JSON"]
323	```
324	
325	Everything below `AgentResponse` in that diagram already exists and is unchanged. `CallToolResult { content, is_error, structured_content }`, `ContentBlock.audience: Vec<Audience>` matching MCP's array-typed `annotations.audience`, the private `*Wire` structs that add the `"type": "text"` discriminator and nest `audience` under `annotations`, and `structured_content` parsed into embedded JSON rather than double-encoded — see [04-mcp-and-napi.md](04-mcp-and-napi.md). The gap is in what `AgentResponse` can hold, not in how it reaches the wire.
326	
327	## Where these types come from
328	
329	`Section`, `SectionBody`, `BudgetSummary`, `SectionCost`, `ProvenanceBlock`, and `ProvenanceEntry` are defined in `michi-core`. michi reaches outside its own workspace for none of them, and in particular it does not depend on `wisp-contracts`.
330	
331	That is a change from an earlier draft of this document, which imported `wisp_contracts::BudgetReport` and `wisp_contracts::Provenance` behind an optional `contracts` feature. michi publishes to crates.io first, so a michi release cannot name a crate that is not published yet — and a feature gate does not fix an ordering problem, since an optional dependency still has to resolve. The vocabulary argument that justified the import is sound and unchanged: `Provenance` and `BudgetReport` are meanings Wisp and monokl must agree on, and they belong in a permissively licensed crate for the harness plugins that cannot link AGPL code. What michi needs is not that meaning. It is the handful of numbers and strings a block renders, which is a smaller thing, and michi's own.
332	
333	The conversion lives in the consumer, which already links both sides:
334	
335	| Consumer | Holds | Converts into |
336	| --- | --- | --- |
337	| `wisp-output` | `wisp_contracts::BudgetReport`, filled by `wisp-context`'s per-section allocator | `BudgetSummary` |
338	| `monokl-agent` | `wisp_contracts::BudgetReport`, filled by its own `apply_budget` | `BudgetSummary` |
339	| both of the above | `wisp_contracts::Provenance`, read off the snapshot the batch ran against | `ProvenanceBlock` |
340	
341	Each conversion is a few dozen lines of field copying in a crate that imports contracts anyway. michi imports it in no build, and learns nothing about how a `Budget` is allocated, what a `WorkspaceFingerprint` hashes, or how `CapabilityPrecision` ranks.
342	
343	`michi renders a budget; it never computes one` is what makes that split hold. Under monokl `08 §7.5` there are two independent producers of a budget report — `monokl-agent` for the CLI and Wisp's `wisp-context` for a briefing — and michi is the only renderer both share. A renderer needs the numbers, not the allocator that produced them, so the numbers are all the envelope takes.
344	
345	**No new feature flag.** All six types are built from types michi already owns, so all six are always compiled and gate 2's small default dependency set is untouched — there is no dependency to gate. `render_json()` stays hand-built and `serde_json`-free: michi owns these shapes, so it emits their keys the way it emits every other key today, and the `budget` and `provenance` JSON keys appear in a default build. The `serde` and `schemars` derives ride the existing optional features and add nothing to the default.
346	
347	## Rules this envelope has to hold
348	
349	| Rule | Why |
350	| --- | --- |
351	| **Never fail closed on overflow.** Partial results, plus counts, plus a refinement hint. Never "no content is returned." | Serena's `find_symbol` returns nothing once `max_answer_chars` is exceeded, leaving the agent to guess a narrower query with no information about what it missed. Partial results plus `total_count` plus a hint naming the refinement operator is strictly more useful, and it is the behavior monokl already has. Wisp D-019 states the same rule for its MCP surface. |
352	| **No pagination cursors on tool results.** | MCP defines `cursor`/`nextCursor` only for list operations — `tools/list` paginates, `tools/call` results have no cursor field, and the 2026-07-28 release candidate does not add one. A cursor on a tool result is a private convention no client will honor. Truncation plus counts plus a hint is the signal that works. |
353	| **TOON for five or more uniform rows; KV for a single receipt.** | TOON's saving comes from stating field names once across many rows. Below roughly five rows the header costs more than the repetition it removes, and a one-item result reads better as `key: value` lines. `SectionBody` carries both so one response can mix them section by section. |
354	| **michi never reads its own TOON back.** | TOON is a rendering target. No render path parses it, and no consumer should: a caller that needs the data as data reads `structured_content`, which carries the same values already typed. Wisp states the same rule for itself. The round-trip parser exists to prove the renderer's output is grammar-valid in property tests, not as a data path. |
355	| **Sections render in insertion order.** | Ordering is a policy the caller measures (Wisp's Prism A/Bs it). michi renders what it was handed, in the order it was handed. |
356	
357	## The Wisp arrangement
358	
359	Wisp's `wisp-output` crate depends on michi through a **local path dependency during coordinated development**, and the publish order runs one way: michi publishes first, and Wisp is not published until michi has a versioned release compatible with Wisp's license and MSRV (Wisp D-006). michi's declared MSRV is `1.93`.
360	
361	Nothing in Wisp gates a michi release, and no consumer integration gates it either (see [ADR 4](../adr/0004-publish-before-consumer-integration.md)). michi publishes first so Wisp can integrate against a versioned dependency, then Wisp can publish its own package. A tagged Git dependency (`michi-core = { git = "…", tag = "michi@0.x.y" }`) remains useful during coordinated development.
362	
363	Licensing is settled, not open. michi is `FSL-1.1-MIT`, matching Wisp's upper layers and Lumen, and monokl carries the same license. With all three on `FSL-1.1-MIT`, the FSL-linking-AGPL redistribution conflict this section used to flag no longer exists.
364	
365	## What this is not
366	
367	**Not a Wisp type, and not a monokl type.** `Section`, `SectionBody`, `BudgetSummary`, and `ProvenanceBlock` name nothing from either domain, and michi's manifest names neither crate. Any orin-dx tool returning heterogeneous results in one call — a status command reporting several subsystems, a CLI answering a compound query — uses the same envelope, and a tool with one list still writes `items()` and never sees a `Section`.
368	
369	**Not a batch executor.** michi has no async runtime and no scheduler. Dedupe, deadlines, snapshot atomicity, and the budget allocation policy are monokl's `query()`; michi receives the outcome and renders it.
370	
371	**Not a budget allocator.** `BudgetSummary` is a record of a decision already made. Which items survive is the caller's algorithm, and michi has no opinion about it.
372	
373	**Not the whole of what monokl asks michi for.** `MICHI-ADJUSTMENTS.md` under monokl's `.claude/plans/` carried a separate set of asks that this document does not cover, and they have since shipped on their own: the five bug fixes (`escape_value` now escapes line breaks instead of dropping them, `toon::list()` headers are the union of every item's fields, the `debug_assert!` arity panic is gone, `AgentResponse` renders a `validate()` failure as a `toon_validation_failed` error body, and `DomainError::render()` escapes newlines in its message and hints), `TruncationOutcome<T>` with `truncate_by_count` and `truncate_by_size` (in place of the sketched `truncate_by_bytes`; see [03 — `truncation`](03-rust-api.md#truncation--what-a-list-cap-cut)), and `DomainError::from_error()` (the `from_error_chain()` ask), which keeps the `source()` chain as `causes`. It explicitly did not propose new `ErrorCode` variants. None of it contradicts this envelope — it was orthogonal work on escaping, truncation, and error rendering.
374	
375	**Not fully clear of michi's third gate yet, and the honest reading matters.** The gate asks for independent real tools that would otherwise hand-roll the identical pattern, and warns that one tool using a pattern heavily is one data point rather than proof. monokl's batch response and Wisp's briefing are two consumers, but Wisp consumes monokl, so they are not independent in the sense the gate means. What carries the case is the survey behind it: across Sourcegraph, Serena, MCP itself, and LSP, nobody attaches a single top-level budget report across multiple result sections — the pattern is absent from the prior art rather than reinvented in it. That is an argument from a gap, which is weaker than the four-for-four evidence `help[]` hints cleared the gate with. Whether that argument carries the gate on its own, whether a third michi consumer has to show up first, or whether the gate is waived for this envelope, is michi's call and nobody else's — Wisp does not clear michi's gates, and michi does not wait on Wisp to attempt it.
376

# The Wisp / monokl Response Envelope

> **Status: Proposed.** This design is not implemented. The inclusion case remains open; see the notes below.

This proposal describes how one `AgentResponse` could carry a monokl batch result or Wisp briefing: named sections, budget and provenance summaries, and index-bearing operation outcomes.

This is the michi half of a contract written down in three places. monokl's `docs/spec/08-library-session-api.md` §7 defines the batch `QueryResponse`; Wisp's `docs/02-architecture-and-contracts.md` §11–§12 defines the MCP surface that renders it; this doc defines what michi must hold for either of them to render through it. Nothing here changes how michi serializes MCP — that part is already right.

## The gap

`AgentResponse` today holds exactly one body. From `crates/michi-core/src/response.rs`:

| Field / type | Line | What it constrains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `toon: ToonOptions` | 34 | One TOON slot: one `type_name` for the whole response, one `fields`/`rows` table |
| `single_item: Vec<KvItem>` | 36 | One KV slot |
| `toon.total_count: Option<usize>` | 34 | One count, for whichever slot renders |
| `enum RenderTarget { Unset, Toon, Kv }` | 18–22 | The two slots are mutually exclusive |
| `toon.max_cell_len: usize` | 34 | Per-cell clamp, TOON path only, set by `truncate_cells_at()` (`DEFAULT_TRUNCATE_CELLS = 200`, line 25) |

`items()` (line 59) sets `target = RenderTarget::Toon`; `kv_items()` (line 108) sets `Kv`; `body()` (line 194) dispatches on `target`, so `render()` reads whichever setter ran last. Calling both silently drops one. A ten-operation batch is not expressible: nine sections disappear with no error and no signal that they existed.

The truncation model has the same shape problem one level down. `truncate_cells_at` clamps a cell. `michi_core::truncate::Truncated { content, original_chars, removed }` describes a string. `michi_core::truncation::TruncationOutcome` describes one list, and `AgentResponse::truncation()` turns it into the response's `totalCount` and one `help[]` line. None describes a response of several parts. The only envelope-level "there is more" signal is `total_count: Option<usize>` plus free-text hints — a bare integer with no per-section breakdown, no relation to a budget, and no way to say why anything was dropped. monokl's `BudgetReport` would have to be flattened into free-text `hint()` calls to reach the agent at all.

## What gets added

Five additions, in dependency order. All five are pure michi and always compiled — nothing here reaches outside the michi workspace for a type. The fourth changes an existing rendered format; the fifth extends `structured_content`.

### 1. Repeatable sections

```rust
/// One named block within a response. A response may hold any number.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct Section {
    /// The section's type name — the identifier at the head of its TOON line, or the KV block's label.
    pub name: String,
    /// The section's contents.
    pub body: SectionBody,
    /// How many items this section actually carries.
    pub returned_count: usize,
    /// How many existed before truncation. `Some(n)` with `n > returned_count` is the "there is more" signal.
    pub total_count: Option<usize>,
    /// Whether producing this section dropped anything.
    pub truncated: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub enum SectionBody {
    /// A uniform list. Rendered through `michi_core::toon::ToonOptions`, per-cell truncation applied.
    Toon { fields: Vec<String>, rows: Vec<Vec<Value>> },
    /// A single receipt or a small set of labelled scalars.
    Kv(Vec<KvItem>),
    /// Prose or an already-rendered fragment michi passes through unchanged.
    Text(String),
}

impl Section {
    pub fn toon(name: impl Into<String>, fields: Vec<String>, rows: Vec<Vec<Value>>) -> Self;
    pub fn kv(name: impl Into<String>, items: Vec<KvItem>) -> Self;
    pub fn text(name: impl Into<String>, body: impl Into<String>) -> Self;
    /// Record the pre-truncation count. `total_count(Some(n))` with `n > returned_count` renders `totalCount: n`.
    pub fn total_count(self, total: Option<usize>) -> Self;
    pub fn truncated(self, truncated: bool) -> Self;
}

impl AgentResponse {
    /// Append a section. Sections render in insertion order — the caller owns ordering,
    /// because ordering is a policy the caller A/Bs (Wisp D-018), not something michi decides.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn section(self, s: Section) -> Self;
}
```

`items()` and `kv_items()` stay, as one-section sugar over the same storage: `items(rows, fields)` becomes `section(Section::toon(self.toon.type_name.clone(), fields, rows))`, `kv_items(items)` becomes `section(Section::kv(self.toon.type_name.clone(), items))`. `RenderTarget` survives as the record of which sugar was used, because `render_toon()` and `render_kv()` are documented to read their named slot unconditionally regardless of the last setter (AC-009) and that behavior has to hold.

Two invariants keep this compatible with what already ships:

- **A response with zero or one section renders byte-for-byte as it does today**, on every one of `render(Text)`, `render(Json)`, `render_toon()`, `render_kv()`, and `render_for()`. The existing `insta` snapshots are the test for this; if any of them moves, the change is wrong. Per the SemVer table in [05-scope-and-quality.md](05-scope-and-quality.md) a rendered-output change is a major bump, and multi-section support does not have to be one.
- **`returned_count` is derived, not trusted, for `Toon` and `Kv` bodies.** Render functions always succeed ([`PRINCIPLES.md`](../../PRINCIPLES.md)), so a `returned_count` disagreeing with `rows.len()` / `items.len()` is clamped to the real length with a `debug_assert!` alongside — the assert fires under `cargo nextest`, the clamp runs in release. `Text` bodies keep whatever the caller declared, since michi cannot count items in prose.

Rendered, a two-section response is just the sections in order:

```text
brief.symbols[12]{name,kind,file,line}:
  RetryPolicy,struct,src/retry/policy.rs,14
  …
totalCount: 40
brief.refs[5]{symbol,file,line}:
  RetryPolicy,src/http/client.rs,88
  …
```

### 2. A response-level budget report

```rust
/// What a budget block renders: the ceilings a caller was working under, what the response cost
/// against them, and what that cost each section. michi owns this type and names nothing from
/// Wisp or monokl.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct BudgetSummary {
    /// Ceilings the caller set. Any of the three may be absent.
    pub max_tokens: Option<u64>,
    pub max_bytes: Option<u64>,
    pub max_items: Option<u64>,
    /// What the response cost, as the caller measured it.
    pub tokens_used: Option<u64>,
    pub bytes_used: Option<u64>,
    /// Whether the budget forced anything out of the response.
    pub truncated: bool,
    /// Per-section accounting, rendered in the order given.
    pub sections: Vec<SectionCost>,
}

/// One section's line in the budget roll-up.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct SectionCost {
    pub name: String,
    pub returned: u64,
    /// How many existed before truncation, when the caller knows.
    pub total: Option<u64>,
    pub truncated: bool,
}

impl AgentResponse {
    /// Attach the response-level budget summary. One per response — a batch has one budget.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn budget(self, b: BudgetSummary) -> Self;
}
```

Every number is an `Option` or a plain counter, so a caller who measured only tokens fills two fields and leaves the rest empty. `u64` rather than `usize` because these values reach JSON, where a platform-dependent width means nothing.

Rendered once, after the last section, as a `budget:` KV block, with a roll-up naming each section's returned and total counts:

```text
budget:
  tokensUsed: 7412
  bytesUsed: 31208
  maxTokens: 8000
  maxBytes: 2097152
  truncated: true
sections[2]{name,returned,total,truncated}:
  brief.symbols,12,40,true
  brief.refs,5,5,false
```

Absent fields are omitted rather than rendered as `null`. The roll-up renders only when the response carries two or more sections. A single-section response already states its count in its own TOON header and `totalCount:` line, and repeating it costs tokens for nothing.

michi renders a budget; it never computes one. Which items survive a budget is the caller's decision — a BM25 cutoff, a reserved-floor allocator, monokl's `apply_budget` degrade-then-drop ladder. Reporting what got cut in a consistent agent-readable shape is the part every caller needs identically, which is exactly the split [`PRINCIPLES.md`](../../PRINCIPLES.md) describes for truncation.

### 3. A provenance slot

```rust
/// What a provenance block renders: a short ordered list of labelled values, plus the one string
/// a freshness check compares. michi assigns no meaning to any of them.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct ProvenanceBlock {
    /// Rendered in order, one `label: value` line each.
    pub entries: Vec<ProvenanceEntry>,
    /// Rendered last when present.
    pub fingerprint: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct ProvenanceEntry {
    pub label: String,
    pub value: String,
}

impl AgentResponse {
    /// Attach the provenance block this response was computed against.
    /// One per response: a batch runs against one snapshot, so it has one provenance.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn provenance(self, p: ProvenanceBlock) -> Self;
}
```

A named pair rather than a `(String, String)` tuple: a tuple serializes as a two-element array, and a third-party reader of `structuredContent` then has nothing to key on.

Rendered as a KV block after `budget:`:

```text
provenance:
  analyzer: rust-analyzer@0.3.2
  observedAt: 1756950000000
  precision: exact
  fingerprint: b3f1c0d2e4a58691
```

One block per response, not one per row — monokl's batch executes against a single `Snapshot`, so one fingerprint covers all N results rather than N fingerprints. Wisp's freshness tool (`wisp_check`) compares exactly the string in `fingerprint`.

The caller picks the labels. `monokl-agent` fills them from the `wisp_contracts::Provenance` its snapshot carries, `wisp-output` from the same type on Wisp's side, and a tool with no analyzer at all fills two entries and no fingerprint. michi renders what it was handed and validates none of it.

Per-edge precision stays out of the envelope. monokl carries `CapabilityPrecision` on each `DependencyEdge` and each `OpBudget` because a batch spanning an `Exact` TypeScript `refs` and a `Structural` Rust `dependents` has no honest single precision. michi renders whatever precision the caller wrote into a row or a provenance entry; it does not reduce several of them to one response-level value, and it has no type that could hold such a value.

### 4. Per-op outcomes: `PartialSuccess`, widened

`idempotency::PartialSuccess` already has the completed/failed/skipped trichotomy a batch needs. What it lacks is position: `Vec<String>` cannot express `results[i]` ↔ `ops[i]`, which is the ordering contract the batch API is built on (DataLoader's rule, restated in monokl §7.4 as an invariant). Reuse the type, widen the identifiers:

```rust
/// One operation's identity within a batch.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct OpRef {
    /// Position in the caller's op slice. `results[index]` answers `ops[index]`.
    pub index: usize,
    /// Display name for the operation.
    pub operation: String,
    /// A stable machine token — `budget_exhausted`, `deadline`, `not_indexed` — never prose.
    /// michi does not define the vocabulary; the caller does.
    pub reason: Option<String>,
}

pub struct PartialSuccess {
    pub completed: Vec<OpRef>,   // was Vec<String>
    pub failed: Vec<FailedOp>,
    pub skipped: Vec<OpRef>,     // was Vec<String>
}

pub struct FailedOp {
    /// Position in the caller's op slice.
    pub index: usize,            // new
    pub operation: String,
    pub reason: String,
    pub recovery: Option<RecoveryHint>,
}
```

The index becomes a rendered column, so the correspondence survives into what the agent reads:

```text
partial_success: "2 completed, 1 failed, 1 skipped"
completed[2]{index,operation}:
  0,symbols
  1,dependents
failed[1]{index,operation,reason}:
  2,refs,"symbol not found: RetryPolicy"
skipped[1]{index,operation,reason}:
  3,search,budget_exhausted
```

**This one is a major bump.** Today's `completed[2]: a,b` inline array becomes `completed[2]{index,operation}:`, so existing rendered output differs — the SemVer table calls that major, and the exact-output tests in `idempotency.rs` (AC-032, AC-033) and the `snapshot_partial_success_full` insta snapshot change with it. There is no external consumer to break yet, which is the cheapest moment this change will ever have.

`exit_code()` is unchanged: `0` when nothing failed, `1` when anything did.

### 5. `structured_content` and a published `outputSchema`

`to_call_tool_result()` already builds `structured_content` from `render(OutputFormat::Json)`. Extend that JSON to carry the envelope:

```json
{
  "body": "…",
  "sections": [
    {
      "name": "brief.symbols",
      "kind": "toon",
      "fields": ["name", "kind", "file", "line"],
      "rows": [["RetryPolicy", "struct", "src/retry/policy.rs", 14]],
      "returnedCount": 12,
      "totalCount": 40,
      "truncated": true
    }
  ],
  "budget": {
    "tokensUsed": 7412,
    "bytesUsed": 31208,
    "maxTokens": 8000,
    "truncated": true,
    "sections": []
  },
  "provenance": {
    "entries": [{ "label": "analyzer", "value": "rust-analyzer@0.3.2" }],
    "fingerprint": "b3f1c0d2e4a58691"
  },
  "hints": ["…"],
  "recovery": [],
  "isError": false
}
```

Every key in that object is camelCase — `returnedCount`, `totalCount`, `tokensUsed`, `maxTokens`, `isError`. The rendered examples above are the specification of that, not an illustration of it: a third-party harness plugin reading this JSON without linking any Rust is a first-class consumer, and `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` on every envelope type is what keeps the spelling stable. Labels inside `provenance.entries` are caller-supplied strings and michi does not case-convert them.

`sections`, `budget`, and `provenance` appear only when their slots are set. A response built entirely through today's API still emits exactly `body`, `hints`, `recovery`, `isError` — the four keys AC-004 pins — so that criterion needs its assertion rewritten from "exactly this set" to "exactly this set, plus the envelope keys whose slots were set", not deleted.

The schema is published through the existing `schemars` feature: `Section`, `SectionBody`, `BudgetSummary`, `SectionCost`, `ProvenanceBlock`, and `ProvenanceEntry` derive `JsonSchema`, and the server declares the result as its tool's `outputSchema`. MCP makes conformance binding once a schema is declared — servers MUST return conforming structured results, clients SHOULD validate — which is the reason to publish one rather than leave the shape implicit. The token-budget caveat in [06-decisions.md](06-decisions.md) still applies: `outputSchema` enters the context window at `tools/list` time, so declare it on always-loaded tools, not on deferred ones.

## The render path

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    S1["Section — Toon"]
    S2["Section — Kv"]
    SN["Section — Text"]
    B["BudgetSummary"]
    P["ProvenanceBlock"]
    HR["hints / recovery"]

    S1 --> AR
    S2 --> AR
    SN --> AR
    B --> AR
    P --> AR
    HR --> AR

    AR["AgentResponse — N sections"]

    AR -->|"render_text()"| text["sections in order, then budget:, provenance:, help[], recovery[]"]
    AR -->|"render(OutputFormat::Json)"| json["sections[], budget, provenance, hints, recovery, isError"]

    text --> block["ContentBlock { audience: [assistant] }"]
    human["human_content()"] --> ublock["ContentBlock { audience: [user] }"]

    block --> ctr["mcp::CallToolResult"]
    ublock --> ctr
    json --> ctr
    ctr --> wire["MCP tools/call JSON"]
```

Everything below `AgentResponse` in that diagram already exists and is unchanged. `CallToolResult { content, is_error, structured_content }`, `ContentBlock.audience: Vec<Audience>` matching MCP's array-typed `annotations.audience`, the private `*Wire` structs that add the `"type": "text"` discriminator and nest `audience` under `annotations`, and `structured_content` parsed into embedded JSON rather than double-encoded — see [04-mcp-and-napi.md](04-mcp-and-napi.md). The gap is in what `AgentResponse` can hold, not in how it reaches the wire.

## Where these types come from

`Section`, `SectionBody`, `BudgetSummary`, `SectionCost`, `ProvenanceBlock`, and `ProvenanceEntry` are defined in `michi-core`. michi reaches outside its own workspace for none of them, and in particular it does not depend on `wisp-contracts`.

That is a change from an earlier draft of this document, which imported `wisp_contracts::BudgetReport` and `wisp_contracts::Provenance` behind an optional `contracts` feature. michi publishes to crates.io first, so a michi release cannot name a crate that is not published yet — and a feature gate does not fix an ordering problem, since an optional dependency still has to resolve. The vocabulary argument that justified the import is sound and unchanged: `Provenance` and `BudgetReport` are meanings Wisp and monokl must agree on, and they belong in a permissively licensed crate for the harness plugins that cannot link AGPL code. What michi needs is not that meaning. It is the handful of numbers and strings a block renders, which is a smaller thing, and michi's own.

The conversion lives in the consumer, which already links both sides:

| Consumer | Holds | Converts into |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wisp-output` | `wisp_contracts::BudgetReport`, filled by `wisp-context`'s per-section allocator | `BudgetSummary` |
| `monokl-agent` | `wisp_contracts::BudgetReport`, filled by its own `apply_budget` | `BudgetSummary` |
| both of the above | `wisp_contracts::Provenance`, read off the snapshot the batch ran against | `ProvenanceBlock` |

Each conversion is a few dozen lines of field copying in a crate that imports contracts anyway. michi imports it in no build, and learns nothing about how a `Budget` is allocated, what a `WorkspaceFingerprint` hashes, or how `CapabilityPrecision` ranks.

`michi renders a budget; it never computes one` is what makes that split hold. Under monokl `08 §7.5` there are two independent producers of a budget report — `monokl-agent` for the CLI and Wisp's `wisp-context` for a briefing — and michi is the only renderer both share. A renderer needs the numbers, not the allocator that produced them, so the numbers are all the envelope takes.

**No new feature flag.** All six types are built from types michi already owns, so all six are always compiled and gate 2's small default dependency set is untouched — there is no dependency to gate. `render_json()` stays hand-built and `serde_json`-free: michi owns these shapes, so it emits their keys the way it emits every other key today, and the `budget` and `provenance` JSON keys appear in a default build. The `serde` and `schemars` derives ride the existing optional features and add nothing to the default.

## Rules this envelope has to hold

| Rule | Why |
| --- | --- |
| **Never fail closed on overflow.** Partial results, plus counts, plus a refinement hint. Never "no content is returned." | Serena's `find_symbol` returns nothing once `max_answer_chars` is exceeded, leaving the agent to guess a narrower query with no information about what it missed. Partial results plus `total_count` plus a hint naming the refinement operator is strictly more useful, and it is the behavior monokl already has. Wisp D-019 states the same rule for its MCP surface. |
| **No pagination cursors on tool results.** | MCP defines `cursor`/`nextCursor` only for list operations — `tools/list` paginates, `tools/call` results have no cursor field, and the 2026-07-28 release candidate does not add one. A cursor on a tool result is a private convention no client will honor. Truncation plus counts plus a hint is the signal that works. |
| **TOON for five or more uniform rows; KV for a single receipt.** | TOON's saving comes from stating field names once across many rows. Below roughly five rows the header costs more than the repetition it removes, and a one-item result reads better as `key: value` lines. `SectionBody` carries both so one response can mix them section by section. |
| **michi never reads its own TOON back.** | TOON is a rendering target. No render path parses it, and no consumer should: a caller that needs the data as data reads `structured_content`, which carries the same values already typed. Wisp states the same rule for itself. The round-trip parser exists to prove the renderer's output is grammar-valid in property tests, not as a data path. |
| **Sections render in insertion order.** | Ordering is a policy the caller measures (Wisp's Prism A/Bs it). michi renders what it was handed, in the order it was handed. |

## The Wisp arrangement

Wisp's `wisp-output` crate depends on michi through a **local path dependency during coordinated development**, and the publish order runs one way: michi publishes first, and Wisp is not published until michi has a versioned release compatible with Wisp's license and MSRV (Wisp D-006). michi's declared MSRV is `1.93`.

Nothing in Wisp gates a michi release, and no consumer integration gates it either (see [ADR 4](../adr/0004-publish-before-consumer-integration.md)). michi publishes first so Wisp can integrate against a versioned dependency, then Wisp can publish its own package. A tagged Git dependency (`michi-core = { git = "…", tag = "michi@0.x.y" }`) remains useful during coordinated development.

Licensing is settled, not open. michi is `FSL-1.1-MIT`, matching Wisp's upper layers and Lumen, and monokl carries the same license. With all three on `FSL-1.1-MIT`, the FSL-linking-AGPL redistribution conflict this section used to flag no longer exists.

## What this is not

**Not a Wisp type, and not a monokl type.** `Section`, `SectionBody`, `BudgetSummary`, and `ProvenanceBlock` name nothing from either domain, and michi's manifest names neither crate. Any orin-dx tool returning heterogeneous results in one call — a status command reporting several subsystems, a CLI answering a compound query — uses the same envelope, and a tool with one list still writes `items()` and never sees a `Section`.

**Not a batch executor.** michi has no async runtime and no scheduler. Dedupe, deadlines, snapshot atomicity, and the budget allocation policy are monokl's `query()`; michi receives the outcome and renders it.

**Not a budget allocator.** `BudgetSummary` is a record of a decision already made. Which items survive is the caller's algorithm, and michi has no opinion about it.

**Not the whole of what monokl asks michi for.** `MICHI-ADJUSTMENTS.md` under monokl's `.claude/plans/` carried a separate set of asks that this document does not cover, and they have since shipped on their own: the five bug fixes (`escape_value` now escapes line breaks instead of dropping them, `toon::list()` headers are the union of every item's fields, the `debug_assert!` arity panic is gone, `AgentResponse` renders a `validate()` failure as a `toon_validation_failed` error body, and `DomainError::render()` escapes newlines in its message and hints), `TruncationOutcome<T>` with `truncate_by_count` and `truncate_by_size` (in place of the sketched `truncate_by_bytes`; see [03 — `truncation`](03-rust-api.md#truncation--what-a-list-cap-cut)), and `DomainError::from_error()` (the `from_error_chain()` ask), which keeps the `source()` chain as `causes`. It explicitly did not propose new `ErrorCode` variants. None of it contradicts this envelope — it was orthogonal work on escaping, truncation, and error rendering.

**Not fully clear of michi's third gate yet, and the honest reading matters.** The gate asks for independent real tools that would otherwise hand-roll the identical pattern, and warns that one tool using a pattern heavily is one data point rather than proof. monokl's batch response and Wisp's briefing are two consumers, but Wisp consumes monokl, so they are not independent in the sense the gate means. What carries the case is the survey behind it: across Sourcegraph, Serena, MCP itself, and LSP, nobody attaches a single top-level budget report across multiple result sections — the pattern is absent from the prior art rather than reinvented in it. That is an argument from a gap, which is weaker than the four-for-four evidence `help[]` hints cleared the gate with. Whether that argument carries the gate on its own, whether a third michi consumer has to show up first, or whether the gate is waived for this envelope, is michi's call and nobody else's — Wisp does not clear michi's gates, and michi does not wait on Wisp to attempt it.

# Architecture decision records

ADRs record decisions that shape the workspace and would be costly or confusing to reverse. Current behavior belongs in [`docs/spec/`](../spec/README.md); workspace structure belongs in [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](../../ARCHITECTURE.md).

Write an ADR when a decision changes crate boundaries, dependencies, public contracts, licensing, security, or another cross-cutting constraint. Do not record local implementation choices or every resolved API detail.

Use `Proposed` while a decision is under review and `Accepted` once it is implemented. To change an accepted decision, add a new ADR that names the one it supersedes; preserve the old record. Cite the source and alternatives considered.

## Decisions

| ADR | Decision | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [0001](0001-async-pipeline-separate-crate.md) | Keep async pipeline execution in its own crate. | Accepted; dependency detail amended by ADR 5 |
| [0002](0002-consumer-integration-before-crates-io.md) | Require an external consumer integration before the first crates.io release. | Superseded by ADR 4 |
| [0003](0003-fsl-1-1-mit-license.md) | License the workspace under FSL-1.1-MIT. | Accepted; amended: `michi-graph` is MIT |
| [0004](0004-publish-before-consumer-integration.md) | Publish an initial version before requiring downstream integration. | Accepted |
| [0005](0005-two-crates-one-version.md) | Publish `michi-core` and `michi-pipeline` on one version; no facade. Amends ADR 1's dependency detail. | Accepted; amended: `michi-graph` joined the group |
| [0006](0006-toon-4-4-conformance.md) | Every agent-facing block is TOON 4.4 encoder output; no michi dialect. | Accepted |
| [0007](0007-pipeline-plans-records-replay.md) | Run pipelines from a validated plan into a strict run record, with one replay rule for retries and resume. | Accepted; amended in 0.5 |

| [0009](0009-v1-positioning-and-criteria.md) | Position michi as a response contract with a pluggable body encoding, and earn 1.0 by use. | Proposed |
# 9. Position michi as a response contract, and earn 1.0 by use

Status: Proposed

## Context

An adversarial review of the README and docs found claims stated more strongly than the evidence supports, and a gap between what michi is for and how it is described. The TOON measurements cover flat, uniform lists of up to 100 rows ([benchmarks](../toon-benchmarks.md)), yet TOON had become the headline. What a tool author gets from michi that is hard to rebuild is the shape around the body: totals, a report of what was cut, next-step hints, recovery steps, structured errors and MCP assembly. The 0.x crates have no external consumer on a published release yet, so a 1.0 would freeze surface nobody has tried.

## Decision

**Positioning.** michi is a response contract for agent-facing tools, with a pluggable body encoding. The contract covers:

- totals (`totalCount`) and the report of what a list cap cut (`truncated`)
- `help[]` next-step hints and `recovery` steps
- structured errors (`DomainError`), status and partial-success reporting
- MCP `CallToolResult` assembly and audience routing

TOON 4.4 is one encoder for the body, and today the only one. It is the right choice for flat, uniform lists that a model reads; it is not claimed to be better for nested data, and it is for models reading tool output, not writing it. Docs describe the contract first and TOON as the default body.

**1.0 criteria.** A crate goes to 1.0 when both hold:

1. At least two independent consumers have run it on a published release for several weeks.
2. What 1.0 promises is what those consumers use. Intended design that no consumer has used yet stays, marked unstable in the docs. Legacy, duplicate and implementation-detail surface is removed or hidden before 1.0.

"Independent" means different tools by different authors, as in [PRINCIPLES.md](../../PRINCIPLES.md) gate 3. Passing tests, completeness and a long feature list are not criteria.

**Versions (decided).** All four packages stay in the `michi` fixed group on one version through 1.0 ([ADR 5](0005-two-crates-one-version.md)), so they reach 1.0 together. A split was considered and rejected by the maintainer, who prefers one version for the whole family. Intended design with no caller yet stays in and is marked unstable in the docs, not removed.

**Deferred past 1.0.** Each needs evidence that does not exist yet:

- **Automatic format selection by data shape.** It needs measurements of format by shape (nested, sparse, long, mixed) and at least two consumers hand-rolling the same selection logic ([PRINCIPLES.md](../../PRINCIPLES.md) gate 3). Callers choose the body today.
- **`Untrusted<T>`-style taint types.** Rejected for now in the trust-model decision in [`06-decisions.md`](../spec/06-decisions.md); no second tool has asked for one.
- **Typed pipeline step outputs** and **scoped or borrowing pipeline steps.** No consumer has run pipelines yet, so the cost of the current shape is unknown.
- **The Wisp and monokl envelope** ([`07-wisp-and-monokl-envelope.md`](../spec/07-wisp-and-monokl-envelope.md)). It stays a proposal.

## Alternatives

- Call 0.7 feature-complete and tag 1.0. Rejected: it freezes surface no consumer has used.
- Keep TOON as the headline. Rejected: the evidence supports a narrower claim, and the contract is what still matters if a better body encoding appears.
- Let `michi-core` reach 1.0 alone while `michi-pipeline` and `michi-graph` stay 0.x. Rejected: one fixed version for the whole family is simpler to release and to explain, and it was decided earlier ([ADR 5](0005-two-crates-one-version.md)).

## Consequences

- README and benchmark docs state the measured scope and what is untested.
- Pre-1.0 breakage stays acceptable. Legacy and duplicate surface can change or go. Intended design stays even without a caller; its stability is documented, not assumed.
- 1.0 may arrive later than the feature set suggests, and it arrives for all four packages together.

## Sources

- [`docs/toon-benchmarks.md`](../toon-benchmarks.md), Limits
- [`PRINCIPLES.md`](../../PRINCIPLES.md), gates 3 and 5
- [ADR 5](0005-two-crates-one-version.md), `callisto.toml`
- `docs/spec/06-decisions.md`, "Resolved 2026-10-24 — Automatic format selection is deferred past 1.0"

# michi spec

The technical reference for `michi-core`, michi's sync primitives crate — what it does, how it's shaped, and why.

See the [documentation map](../README.md) for the role of this reference and related design records.

## Reading order

| Doc | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| [01-overview-and-setup.md](01-overview-and-setup.md) | What michi is, why it exists, what's deliberately out of scope, who consumes it, `Cargo.toml`, crate layout |
| [02-toon-format.md](02-toon-format.md) | The TOON grammar — the agent-facing list format |
| [03-rust-api.md](03-rust-api.md) | Every `michi-core` module: `toon`, `kv`, `hints`, `truncate`, `truncation`, `empty`, `error`, `idempotency`, `resilience`, `status`, `recovery`, `response`, `pipeline`, `audience`, `telemetry` |
| [04-mcp-and-napi.md](04-mcp-and-napi.md) | The `mcp` module, the NAPI/npm boundary, and the builder-across-FFI problem |
| [05-scope-and-quality.md](05-scope-and-quality.md) | What's formalized vs. what stays in your app, feature flags, versioning, performance, testing |
| [06-decisions.md](06-decisions.md) | Open questions and API design rationale |
| [08-pipeline-execution.md](08-pipeline-execution.md) | `michi-pipeline`: step plans, the replay rule, the status model, the run record, scheduling, cancellation, keyed breakers, the retry budget, the observer and resume |
| [09-graph.md](09-graph.md) | `michi-graph`: the MIT dependency-graph crate — building, validation, order, layers, ready sets, violations, and how `michi-pipeline` uses it |

New to the crate? Read 01 → 02 → 03 in order — that's the whole mental model. Read 04–06 and 08 as needed.

## Proposed designs

These documents describe possible future work, not available APIs.

| Doc | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| [07-wisp-and-monokl-envelope.md](07-wisp-and-monokl-envelope.md) | Multi-section response envelope for Wisp and monokl: `Section`, michi's own `BudgetSummary` and `ProvenanceBlock` slots, index-bearing per-op outcomes, `structuredContent` and `outputSchema`; inclusion case remains open |
| [10-pipeline-effects.md](10-pipeline-effects.md) | Amendment to 08: what happened to a failed step's effect (not applied or unknown), so resume never repeats one blindly; an opt-in precheck that adopts effects already in place; durable starts that close the crash gap |

## Known gaps

**TOON retrieval accuracy is measured on Claude and one OpenAI model.** On Claude Haiku, Sonnet and Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Sol TOON matches JSON and Markdown; Gemini and open-weight models, much longer lists and open-ended tasks are untested. See [TOON benchmarks](../toon-benchmarks.md) and [the research note](../research/toon-retrieval-accuracy.md).

**No external consumer has integrated against a published Michi version yet.** Published releases (from 0.3.1) provide that version; downstream integration is the next validation step (see [ADR 4](../adr/0004-publish-before-consumer-integration.md)).

- [07-wisp-and-monokl-envelope.md](07-wisp-and-monokl-envelope.md) is a proposal for one possible integration; none of its APIs are built yet.
- A consumer may use a tagged Git dependency during development, then validate against the published crate. Any issues can inform a follow-up release.

**`cli` isn't a Cargo feature of this crate at all.** Reserved name for future terminal-aware rendering, in a separate crate, not implemented.

**Plan 2 (the async execution layer) doesn't exist as code in this crate — but `pipeline`'s half has landed as its own crate.**

- `pipeline` has a real, tested data type and `render()` in `michi-core` — always compiled.
- The actual executor exists too, just not in this crate: `crates/michi-pipeline` ships `Plan`, `execute`/`resume` returning a `RunRecord`, a keyed `BreakerRegistry` and `CancellationToken`. It depends on `michi-core` (for `StepStatus`, the `Pipeline` view and `resilience` retry config and budget) and `michi-graph` (dependency validation and order), and isn't re-exported through `michi-core`.
- `fuzzy`, `cache`, and `cli` don't exist anywhere in the workspace at all — not even as stubs. Earlier placeholder stub files were deliberately deleted; see [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](../../ARCHITECTURE.md).
- Each remaining piece lands as its own crate when it's actually built, per the same pattern `michi-pipeline` followed.
- 01–06 cover Plan 1, the pure-primitives crate, and 07 proposes an extension to it; `michi-pipeline`'s API is [08-pipeline-execution.md](08-pipeline-execution.md) and `michi-graph`'s is [09-graph.md](09-graph.md).

## Companion docs

- [`../../PRINCIPLES.md`](../../PRINCIPLES.md) — what belongs in michi and why, plus how work here gets done
- [`../../ARCHITECTURE.md`](../../ARCHITECTURE.md) — the design in prose, one level up from this spec's API detail
- [`../../CONTRIBUTING.md`](../../CONTRIBUTING.md) — how to actually send a PR
- [`../adr/README.md`](../adr/README.md) — durable architectural decisions
- [`../research/README.md`](../research/README.md) — open questions that need evidence

# Effects, precheck and durable starts (amendment to 08)

Status: **implemented in 0.5.** The rules are in [08-pipeline-execution.md](08-pipeline-execution.md) and the decision record, including the choices made while building it, is "Two facts per failure" in [06-decisions.md](06-decisions.md). This document stays as the rationale; where it and 08 differ, 08 is current. The differences are listed under "Deviations" at the end.

## The problem

michi's promise is that retries and resume never blindly repeat work that may already have taken effect. Three paths break it today:

1. **A definitive failure is re-run on resume.** A non-idempotent step can commit its effect and then return `Failed { retryable: false }`. It ends `Failed`, and resume runs every `Failed` step again, so the effect repeats. A consumer probe observed two commits. HTTP 500 has the same problem: it is classed as definitive, but a server error says nothing about whether the request was applied (RFC 9110 §15.6).
2. **`retryable: false` is read as "not applied".** It only says retrying would not help. Whether the effect landed is a separate fact, and the model has nowhere to record it.
3. **A start that was never recorded.** If `on_step_started` fails to save the in-flight marker (it panics, or its storage write fails), the scheduler dispatches the step anyway. After a crash, the rebuilt record shows it `Pending` and resume runs it again.

docs/spec/06-decisions.md:506:- **Retry safety:** `DomainError.retryable` was documented as "safe to retry", yet `Timeout` and `ExternalFailure` defaulted to `true`, so `DomainError::new(Timeout, "POST /charge timed out")` told an agent to retry a request that may have charged the card. `retryable` now means calling again is expected to help without repeating an effect, and defaults to `true` only for `RateLimited` and `Unavailable`, which mean the request was not processed. `Timeout` and `ExternalFailure` default to `false`; a caller that knows the operation is idempotent passes `.retryable(true)`. This matches michi-pipeline, which sets `retryable` explicitly (HTTP 500 → `ExternalFailure`, not retryable; a non-idempotent ambiguous outcome is wrapped and not retryable) and the proposed effect model in `10-pipeline-effects.md` (implemented in 0.5), where retrying an `Unknown` effect needs an idempotent step. A timeout that is not marked retryable is classed `ErrorClass::Ambiguous`, not `Internal`: it is neither the caller's fault nor an internal error, and an agent needs to know the operation may have taken effect. It carries the hint `MAY_HAVE_TAKEN_EFFECT_HINT` until the caller marks it retryable. `ExternalFailure` stays `Internal` with no automatic hint, because it covers failures where "may have taken effect" would be noise (a failed local walk); callers that know better add a hint, as michi-pipeline does for an ambiguous outcome. `is_retryable_status` keeps 502 and 504 in its set (transport retry loops expect them) but documents that only 429 and 503 say the request was not processed. Breaking for code that relied on the old default, so it ships in a minor release.

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Versioning

The Model Context Protocol uses string-based version identifiers following the format
`YYYY-MM-DD`, to indicate the last date backwards incompatible changes were made.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The protocol version will *not* be incremented when the
> protocol is updated, as long as the changes maintain backwards compatibility. This allows
> for incremental improvements while preserving interoperability.

## Revisions

Revisions may be marked as:

* **Draft**: in-progress specifications, not yet ready for consumption.
* **Current**: the current protocol version, which is ready for use and may continue to
  receive backwards compatible changes.
* **Final**: past, complete specifications that will not be changed.

The **current** protocol version is [**2026-07-28**](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28.md).

## Feature States

Individual features of the specification may additionally be marked as
**Deprecated** under the
[feature lifecycle and deprecation policy](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/community/feature-lifecycle.md):
the feature remains part of the specification, but is scheduled for removal.
Deprecated features document a migration path (or state that none is required)
and remain in the specification for at least twelve months, or at least
ninety days under the policy's
[expedited-removal exception](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/community/feature-lifecycle.md#expedited-removal),
before they become eligible for removal, after which they may be **Removed**
in a future revision.

Features that are currently Deprecated are listed in the
[deprecated features registry](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/deprecated.md).

## Negotiation

Every request declares the protocol version it is using via the
`io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion` key in its
[`_meta`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/index#meta) field, and the server accepts or
rejects each request independently. On Streamable HTTP, the same value is also carried
in the
[`MCP-Protocol-Version` header](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http#protocol-version-header).
Clients and servers **MAY** support multiple protocol versions simultaneously.

If the server does not support the requested version, it responds with an
[`UnsupportedProtocolVersionError`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning#protocol-version-negotiation)
listing the versions it does support. The client can then retry the request with a
mutually supported version, or surface an error to the user if none exists.

Clients that want to select a version up front can call
[`server/discover`](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/discover), a mandatory RPC that
returns the server's supported protocol versions, capabilities, and identity in a
single request. Calling it is optional: a client is free to send any request directly
and handle a version error if one comes back.

For interoperability with servers and clients that implement the
handshake-based protocol revisions (`2025-11-25` and earlier), see
[Backward Compatibility](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/versioning.md#backward-compatibility-with-initialization-based-versions).

    s = open(p).read()
    assert old in s, (p, old[:40])
    open(p, 'w').write(s.replace(old, new, count))

open(p, 'w').write(s)

cat >> docs/spec/06-decisions.md <<'EOF'

### Resolved 2026-11-15 — Envelope implementation deviations (gate 5)

[ADR 10](../adr/0010-response-envelope-accepted.md) accepts the envelope in [07](07-wisp-and-monokl-envelope.md). Building it departed from the spec text in these places; the code and [03-rust-api.md](03-rust-api.md) are current.

- **`returned_count` is derived, with no clamp and no `debug_assert!`.** Spec 07 section 1 clamped a wrong count and asserted in debug builds, so debug and release disagreed. `Section::count()` computes `rows.len()` or `items.len()` for `Toon` and `Kv`; only `Text` keeps the declared value. The `returned_count` setter is ignored for `Toon` and `Kv`.
- **Render order puts the `items()` / `kv_items()` content first**, then sections, then `budget:`, `provenance:`, `help[]`, `recovery[]`. The spec only described sections. An untouched slot renders nothing once any section, budget or provenance is set, so `AgentResponse::new("t").budget(b)` has no `t: []` line.
- **The budget roll-up counts blocks, not only sections.** It renders at two or more blocks, counting the `items()` / `kv_items()` slot when it has content. The spec said "two or more sections".
- **Several cut sections no longer repeat `truncated[N]`; several totals no longer repeat `totalCount`.** Slice 1 emitted one block per section, which repeats a root key (TOON 4.4 section 14.3). One block with cuts or a total renders as the single-slot form. Two or more render one table each, `truncated[N]{section,row,field,removed}:` and `totalCount[N]{section,total}:`, after the last block. Rejected alternative: a `section` column always, which would change what one section renders compared with `items()`. michi's own "Cut cells are listed" help line is added once.
- **Names are the caller's to keep distinct.** Section names, KV keys across KV sections, and the names `budget`, `provenance` and `sections` are root keys. michi does not rename or reject them.
- **The spec's `observedAt: 1756950000000` example was wrong.** A string that looks like a number must be quoted in TOON (section 7.2), and the code does so. The example now reads `observedAt: "1756950000000"`.
- **The roll-up table has `null` for an unknown total**, because a table row needs a value in every column. Absent scalar fields in `budget:` are omitted.
- **JSON section shapes the spec left open:** `kind` is `toon`, `kv` or `text`; `kv` carries `items` as `{key, value}` objects, `text` carries `text`; `totalCount` is the declared value when set (text hides it unless it exceeds the count); rows hold full values, not cell-capped ones. The slot content is in `body` only.
- **JSON stays hand-built** and `serde_json`-free in the default build.
- **The strict test decoder** learned one-level nested objects (for `budget:` and `provenance:`) and stopped treating a row indented with U+2028 as a `#` comment line. That was a decoder bug, found by the new property test, not a renderer one.
- **Not built:** the published `outputSchema` of spec 07 section 5 (the `schemars` derives exist), and spec 07 section 4 (`PartialSuccess` index), which lands in its own PR.
EOF
